t.en:
Neo-Moscow in 2087 greeted its visitors with the usual acid rain. The neon glare of the skyscrapers bled into the puddles, and passenger drones droned overhead. Thirty-four-year-old Maya Severova stood before the massive glass doors of the Helios corporation, shaking the drops off her beige trench coat. The collar of her grey sweater was turned up high, setting off her fair skin and hiding a small burn scar on her left cheek from the cold wind — an old souvenir of a failed experiment. A former robotics engineer and now a private detective, she had not come here out of any love for corporate intrigue.

The case smelled of the impossible, and Maya adored debunking miracles.

“The lab was locked from the inside, Ms. Severova,” the head of security chattered nervously, scurrying after her down the snow-white corridor. “Kai, our newest assistant model, simply evaporated! The security cameras recorded nothing but an empty corridor all night. Nobody went in, nobody came out.”

Maya stopped short, smoothed her short, straight black hair — damp from the rain and cut in a perfect bob — and gave the security man a calm look with her brown eyes.

“Androids weighing a hundred and fifty kilos don’t know how to evaporate, even if they’re very tired of working at your lovely company,” the detective remarked dryly.

They entered the lab. The air smelled of ozone and hot metal. A torn diagnostic cable lay forlornly on the empty assembly stand. Maya stepped closer, studying the floor. Amid the sterile cleanliness one detail stood out: a chain of barely visible oily marks leading to the ventilation grate. The grate itself, however, was firmly bolted from inside the room. Maya slowly crouched down and took from the pocket of her trench coat a magnifier with a built-in analyzer.

en: The analyzer identified the traces as fresh human blood.
The bolts on the grate suddenly began to slowly unscrew.
A tiny holographic inscription flickered on a bolt head.
A bright red optic suddenly flashed from the vent.
The oil drops passed straight through the solid metal.
